outcomes.original: Filing step: Confirm formula retail status in writing with SF Planning Department via pre-application meeting or zoning counter inquiry. What to say: Request a written determination of whether Super Duper Burgers' 11 locations and standardized trade dress meet Planning Code Section 303.1(b) formula retail thresholds in the NCD-Inner Sunset district. Provide the business name, number of locations, franchise structure (if any), and any variations in menu, layout or branding across locations. Ask whether Planning Code Section 730 allows formula retail restaurants by Conditional Use or prohibits them, and cite the Yi Fang CUA (2019-006316CUA) as a comparable formula retail restaurant approval in the district. If formula retail applies, ask whether First Year Free fee waivers under Planning Code Section 351 are available for a new storefront business.
outcomes.note: Records confirm Yi Fang CUA was a formula retail restaurant approval in NCD-Inner Sunset, but don't state the content of Planning Code sections 303.1(b), 730, or 351.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If formula retail CUA is required, file the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning, including the pre-application meeting summary, project narrative, site plan, elevation drawings, and neighborhood outreach plan. What to say: Frame the application as a fast-casual restaurant serving the Inner Sunset's established dining corridor, with 2,231 square feet under the 2,500 sq ft size threshold. Emphasize that restaurant use is principally permitted in the district and that the space has continuous restaurant history since 2003, most recently approved in 2020 as a limited restaurant. Describe Super Duper as a local Bay Area chain (founded in San Francisco) offering fresh, quality burgers in a neighborhood-friendly format, not a national formula retail chain. Commit to the standard eating-and-drinking conditions: daily sidewalk maintenance within one block, soundproofing, odor control, interior trash storage, and a community liaison. Provide letters of support from the existing business (if staying) and from nearby merchants if possible. State operating hours (if not closing after 2 a.m., note that and cite Plannin…
outcomes.note: The CUA record is for 645 Irving St (83m away), not the report address at 737 Irving St. The zoning record shows restaurant permission as unknown, not principally permitted.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Complete the 30-day posted notice and 300-foot mailed notice for the CUA, and attend the pre-hearing community meeting required by Planning. What to say: Post the yellow notice at the site for 30 days and photograph it weekly for proof. Mail notice to all property owners and occupants within 300 feet using Planning's mailing list. At the community meeting (typically held 2–4 weeks before the hearing), present the project as a local fast-casual restaurant with quality ingredients, a family-friendly atmosphere, and a commitment to being a good neighbor. Address concerns about trash, noise, odor and parking by describing the operational controls: trash stored inside, limited cooking (no deep fryers), soundproofed interior, and no customer parking requirement in the transit-rich Inner Sunset. Offer the community liaison's contact information and invite neighbors to visit an existing Super Duper location.
outcomes.note: The record does not describe 30-day posted notice, 300-foot mailed notice, or pre-hearing community meeting requirements.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Attend the Planning Commission hearing and present the project for Conditional Use Authorization under Planning Code Section 303. What to say: At the hearing, emphasize the Planning Code Section 303(c) findings: the use is necessary or desirable for the neighborhood (the Inner Sunset has 43 food businesses within 500 feet, showing demand); it will not be detrimental to nearby properties (standard conditions mitigate impacts); and it is consistent with the General Plan's economic development and neighborhood commercial policies. Note that the only comparable formula retail restaurant CUA in the district (Yi Fang, 645 Irving St) was approved with standard conditions and no special restrictions. If Planning staff recommends approval, thank the Commission and commit to all recommended conditions. If there is organized opposition, respond calmly: reiterate the operational commitments, offer to meet with concerned neighbors post-approval, and note the space's long restaurant history.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After Commission approval, wait out the 30-day appeal period and obtain the final CUA approval letter from SF Planning. What to say: The Commission's motion granting the CUA becomes final 30 days after the hearing date unless an appeal is filed with the Board of Supervisors. If an appeal is filed, coordinate with Planning staff and legal counsel to prepare a response and attend the Board hearing. Once the 30-day period expires with no appeal, request the final approval letter from Planning and attach it to the building permit application.
outcomes.note: The record does not describe the 30-day appeal period, appeal procedures, or post-approval steps mentioned in the playbook step.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If formula retail does not apply, file the building permit application with DBI, including the CUA approval (if one was required) and architect-stamped plans for tenant improvements. What to say: Submit the building permit with a cover letter stating that restaurant use is principally permitted in the NCD-Inner Sunset per Planning Code Section 730, the space has continuous restaurant history since 2003, and the CUA (if required) is attached. Include plans stamped by a licensed architect showing the kitchen layout, hood and fire suppression system, ADA accessibility, restrooms, and finishes. Route the application to Planning (for zoning review), DPH (for plan check), and the Fire Department (if the occupant load is 50 or more). Request expedited review if the space was recently a restaurant and the TI scope is limited to cosmetic upgrades and equipment replacement.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the DPH plan check application concurrently with or before the building permit, including kitchen plans, equipment list, menu, and finishes schedule. What to say: File the plan check through the DPH portal with the Business Account Number (BAN), the federal tax ID, and scaled drawings of the kitchen. Describe the menu (burgers, fries, shakes) and cooking methods (griddle, limited fryer, no charbroiler) to show this is limited cooking. List all equipment: griddle, prep tables, three-compartment sink, hand sinks, refrigeration, and the hood and fire suppression system. Show that surfaces are smooth, sealed and cleanable per the California Retail Food Code. Schedule a pre-submittal meeting with the DPH plan reviewer if the space layout has changed since 2020, and ask whether the existing hood and grease interceptor are adequate for the new concept.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After DPH plan approval and building permit issuance, complete construction and schedule the DPH pre-opening inspection and the DBI final inspection. What to say: Book the DPH pre-opening inspection at least two weeks in advance with the assigned plan reviewer. Before the inspection, walk the space against the DPH checklist: hot and cold running water at all sinks, hand soap and towels at hand sinks, all surfaces sealed, food contact surfaces smooth and cleanable, thermometers in refrigeration, sanitizer test strips available, and a certified food manager on site. The inspector will verify that the built space matches the approved plans. After DPH approval, schedule the DBI final and the Fire Department final (if required), then apply for the Health Permit to Operate. The permit is issued after all inspections pass and the $470 application fee is paid.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $15,000. Notes: The timeline and cost assume a Conditional Use Authorization is required for formula retail and is approved. CUA filing to Commission approval: 120 to 300 days, as shown by the Yi Fang formula retail restaurant CUA at 645 Irving St which took 279 days from filing (3 May 2019) to approval (6 February 2020). The range reflects variation in hearing scheduling, environmental review (categorical exemption expected), and whether discretionary review or an appeal is filed. The CUA application fee was $2,747 on the 2023-24 schedule and is CPI-adjusted annually (roughly $3,100 now for a no-construction CUA; fees rise with construction cost). Building permit fees ($800 to $15,000) and DPH plan check ($828 to $2,207) are additional and depend on construction valuation and TI scope. If formula retail does not apply, the over-the-counter building permit and health permit path takes 14 to 120 days at lower cost. This timeline is to approval of the CUA and issuance of permits, not to opening; construction, final inspections and permit-to-operate issuance add 2 to 4 months after permit issuance.
